objective: Assess suicide risk directly when ideation is present, including lethality: whether there is a detailed plan, access to means, past attempts, current mental state and social support
secondaryObjectives: Know that suicidal ideation ranges from fleeting passive thoughts to a detailed plan with timing and method, and that depression and substance use are its most common drivers
Supporting the client with an unexpected altered body image

sources.cite: NIMH, Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (ASQ) Toolkit, information sheet: four questions and a fifth acuity question asked after any yes; a yes to it is an acute positive, 'imminent risk', that needs a STAT safety and full mental health evaluation, and the patient 'cannot leave until evaluated for safety'; a non-acute positive needs a brief suicide safety assessment; refusing to answer counts as positive
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 in NIMH's PDF (summarizing fetch with short quotes). The four questions: a wish to be dead, feeling others would be better off, thoughts of suicide in the past week, any attempt ever. 'Clinical judgment can always override a negative screen.' Validated for youth and adult medical patients, including adult medical inpatients (Horowitz et al., Psychosomatics 2020); the toolkit has emergency department, inpatient and outpatient pathways (NIMH adult toolkit page, read the same day). The questions are paraphrased in the sim.

sources.cite: NIMH, Adult ASQ Toolkit: Brief Suicide Safety Assessment guides, nursing scripts and suicide risk screening pathways for the emergency department, the inpatient medical/surgical unit and outpatient primary care and specialty clinics
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (summarizing fetch): an index page; the pathways themselves were not opened, so what each setting does after a positive screen is taken from the information sheet.

sources.cite: The Columbia Lighthouse Project, Columbia Protocol (C-SSRS) triage page: 'the most worrisome answers are a recent (past month) yes to items 4 or 5' (intent, intent with a plan) 'and/or any recent (3 months) behavior'; next steps 'are setting specific', and 'interventions should be changed to reflect your individual resources and policies'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (summarizing fetch with quotes; page last modified 2024-03-22). The screener's items, relayed from the NCMHCE session (read 2026-11-11): wish to be dead; suicidal thoughts; thoughts with method; intent without plan; intent with plan; suicidal behavior.

sources.cite: The Joint Commission, R3 Report Issue 18: National Patient Safety Goal for suicide prevention, NPSG.15.01.01 (effective 2019-07-01): EP1 environmental risk assessment; EP2 screen 'using a validated screening tool'; EP3 an assessment that 'directly asks about suicidal ideation, plan, intent, suicidal or self-harm behaviors'; EP4 document the risk level and the mitigation plan; EP5-EP7 policies for monitoring, discharge counseling and follow-up
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (summarizing fetch with quotes; issue dated 2019-11-20, updated 2025-12-03). The report names one-to-one monitoring as a key protocol on nonpsychiatric units; it does not itself require it, so the observation level in each sim is the facility's policy.

sources.cite: SAMHSA, SAFE-T: Suicide Assessment Five-Step Evaluation and Triage (PEP24-01-036): identify risk and protective factors, conduct a suicide inquiry, determine the risk level and interventions, and document a treatment plan

brief.situation: Frank Delgado, 58 (a fictional client), is on a medical-surgical unit on day 2 after a below-knee amputation for a diabetic foot infection. He was a long-haul truck driver and lives alone since his divorce. He drinks 'a few beers most nights'. At 19:30 he refuses his dinner and says, 'I'm done. I mean it. I'm not living like this.' The hospital screens clients with a validated suicide screening tool when there is a cue. You are his registered nurse, with four other clients; you have about 30 minutes.
handover: Day 2 after a below-knee amputation; incision clean; pain controlled; glucose in range.
Unit policy: a positive screen gets constant observation and a room check until the provider's brief suicide safety assessment.
howItWorks: Choose what to ask and how to respond from the action groups. Frank answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the clock by the minutes that exchange took.
His trust, distress and how much he discloses change with what you say.
Your time ends at 30 minutes. Afterward you write a short risk formulation, then document the risk level and disposition.

source.note: About 30 minutes with one client in a five-client medical-surgical assignment (author's scenario timing).
How trust and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a patient.

checkIn.label: Sit down: 'You said you're done. Tell me what you mean.'

effects.log: You sit at eye level and ask him what he means.

effects.finding: "Thirty years driving. Who hires a trucker with one foot?"

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: He nods once. "Yeah. Everything I was."

normalize.label: Normalize: 'When someone says that, I always ask some direct questions. It's safe to answer.'

effects.log: You explain that you ask direct questions whenever someone says that, and that it is safe to answer.

screen.label: Screen with the NIMH Ask Suicide-Screening Questions (the four questions)
screen.why: He has answered; go on to the follow-up questions.

effects.log: You ask the four screening questions directly.

then.finding: "Yes. Yes. Yes, since they told me about the foot." And, quietly: "Once, after the divorce. Ten years ago."

then.log: Positive screen: a wish to be dead, feeling a burden, suicidal thoughts this week, and a past attempt ten years ago.

then.finding: "Forget I said it." (Not yet enough trust to answer honestly.)

formulation.question: Write your risk formulation for Frank: his risk level and why, and what you put in place.

parts.label: Risk level and reasons
parts.criteria: Names an acute positive screen: thoughts right now, a plan for after discharge, access at home, a past attempt, low mood, poor sleep and heavier drinking, sudden loss of work and body image, living alone; protective: his daughter and friend.
parts.modelAnswer: Acute positive: thoughts of killing himself right now, a plan for after discharge and access at home. A past attempt, months of low mood, poor sleep and heavier drinking, a sudden loss of his work and body image, and living alone all raise the risk. His daughter and friend are protective.

parts.label: What was put in place
parts.criteria: Names constant observation, a room check, the provider called now with discharge held, a psychiatry consult and the handoff.
parts.modelAnswer: Constant observation and a checked room under the policy; the provider called now for the safety assessment; discharge on hold; psychiatry consulted; the charge nurse told and the handoff written.

scoring.modelReasoning: Ideation is on a range from passive thoughts to a plan with timing. When it is present, the nurse asks directly about thoughts right now, a plan, access, past attempts, mental state and supports, never asking for a description of a method. A plan with access and a past attempt makes this imminent risk: constant observation, a room check, the provider now and discharge held.
